0x1a23c.why: `movea.l $6(a1),a0; move.b $1(a1),(a0)` and back to 0x1A3E0. The command carries both the value at +1 and where to put it at +6.

0x1a248.name: add the command's byte through its own pointer
0x1a248.why: `movea.l $6(a1),a0; move.b $1(a1),d0; add.b d0,(a0)` and back to 0x1A3E0. The additive sibling of 0x1A23C.

0x1a256.name: call through the pointer at offset 6 of the command
0x1a256.why: `movea.l $6(a1),a0; jsr (a0)` then `bra.w $1a3e0`, the tail every case of this command table returns through. The command carries its own handler.

0x1a260.name: mark every record whose field 0x15 matches the command's byte
0x1a260.why: walks the sixteen 0x60-byte records, comparing `$15(a2,d0.w)` against the byte at +1 of the command and writing 0xFF into `$12(a2,d0.w)` on a match, then back to the command tail at 0x1A3E0.

0x1a284.name: mark every record whose field 0x12 matches, when the command is kind eight
0x1a284.why: indexes the ten-byte command records by the byte at +1, requires the opcode there to be 8, and then walks the sixteen 0x60-byte records writing 0xFF into `$12(a2,d0.w)` wherever it already equals the command's byte at +2.

0x1a2c6.name: mark every record on the list the command's two nibbles select
0x1a2c6.why: splits the byte at +1 into two nibbles: the high one indexes the six-byte records at 0x19CE4 and its field +5 is added to the low one, and that sum indexes the thirteen list heads at 0x3E3D12. It then walks the list, writing 0xFF into each record's field 0x12 and following the link at offset zero.

0x1a318.name: silence the records the command names, and drain the ring
0x1a318.why: two nearly identical walks over the sixteen 0x60-byte records: one matches field 0x12 against the byte at +2 of the ten-byte command record the byte at +1 selects, the other matches field 0x15 against that byte directly. A match clears +0x5C, sets +0x58 to 0x100 and +0x5A to 0xD000, and writes 0xFE into +0x12. A third entry pushes the byte into the ring at 0x1A19A.

0x1a58a.name: read the channel's value, from the table above six or the jump table below
0x1a58a.why: a selector of 6 or more indexes the bytes at 0x3E36AC by selector minus six and sign-extends; below six it jumps through the five-way table at 0x1A5BE, whose cases are the field reads at 0x1A5C8 to 0x1A5E0. Anything above four in that range falls to the field 0x5E read at 0x1A5E6.

0x1a5c8.name: read the word at offset 0x1C and shift it right three
0x1a5c8.why: `move.w $1c(a0),d0; lsr.w #$3,d0; andi.b #$ff,d0` and into signExtendByteLong at 0x1A5EA - so the top five bits of the field become the answer.

0x1a5d4.name: sign-extend the byte at offset 0x19 of the record
0x1a5d4.why: `move.b $19(a0),d0; bra.b $1a5ea` - one field read and the shared sign extension. A jump-table case; the offset is what the case selects.

0x1a5da.name: sign-extend the byte at offset 0x1B of the record

0x1a5e0.name: sign-extend the byte at offset 0x16 of the record

0x1a5e6.name: sign-extend the byte at offset 0x5E of the record
0x1a5e6.why: `move.b $5e(a0),d0` and falls into signExtendByteLong at 0x1A5EA. The offset is the whole routine.

0x1a5f0.name: run one channel's script to its next rest
0x1a5f0.why: clears the flag at 0x3E36EC and keeps the record in the frame, then enters the script reader's loop at 0x1B054 with 0x3E36E2 and 0x3E36DA - the note table and the current instrument - in registers.

0x1a704.name: raise flag bit one and clear the two counters at 0x3E3706
0x1a704.why: `ori.b #$2,(a4)` then `clr.w` into 0x3E3706 and a zero byte into 0x3E3708, and out through 0x1B050.

0x1a71a.name: quarter the record's word at 0x22, or clear the counters
0x1a71a.why: with the word at +8 zero it falls to 0x1B050 or to 0x1A704 depending on the frame long; otherwise, when neither of bits 1 and 2 of 0x3E36D4 is set, `asr.w #$2` halves the word at +0x22 twice.

0x1a740.name: total the channel's pitch, offset and bend into the long at d5
0x1a740.why: the word at +8 always; and when the frame long is set, the words at +0x1C and +0x22 as well. The three components of a channel's final pitch.

0x1a808.name: clear the frame byte five below a6, then continue at 0x1B048
0x1a808.why: `clr.b -$5(a6); bra.w $1b048`. One field of the caller's frame and a tail jump.

0x1a810.name: read two script bytes and dispatch opcodes 0x80 to 0xBB
0x1a810.why: takes two bytes through the cursor at +4 of the record, stepping it each time, and jumps through the word table at 0x1A848 for a first byte between 0x80 and 0xBB; anything else goes to 0x1AE44. The second byte is left in d4, which is the operand every case there reads.

0x1abc6.name: copy field 0x5D into 0x5E, and the arithmetic that precedes it
0x1abc6.why: the shared tail `move.b $5d(a2),$5e(a2); bra.w $1b048`, reached from four entries above it that first apply d4 to field 0x5D - subtract, and, or, eor - and from a fifth that advances the script cursor at +4 by four times the field less one.

0x1abf6.name: take the next byte of the script and step its pointer
0x1abf6.why: `movea.l $4(a2),a0; addq.l #$1,$4(a2); moveq #$0,d3; move.b (a0),d3` - reads through the cursor at +4 of the record and advances it, which is what makes this a script reader rather than a field read.

0x1ac02.name: read a three-byte big-endian operand from the script
0x1ac02.why: three passes of `movea.l $4(a2),a0; addq.l #$1,$4(a2); move.b (a0),d0` shifted by 8, 0x10 and 0 into d3 - the cursor at +4 stepping once per byte, most significant first.

0x1ace0.name: sign-extend field 0x5D of the record into the word at 0x1C

0x1acec.name: copy field 0x5D of the record into field 0x19
0x1acec.why: `move.b $5d(a2),$19(a2); bra.w $1b048`. One field to another and the shared tail.

0x1acf6.name: sign-extend field 0x5D of the record into the word at 0x1A
0x1acf6.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d1; ext.w d1; move.w d1,$1a(a2)`. Field 0x1A where 0x1ACE0 writes 0x1C.

0x1ad04.name: copy field 0x5D into 0x16 unless field 0x12 is 0xFE
0x1ad04.why: `cmpi.b #$fe,$12(a2)` returns straight to the tail; otherwise `move.b $5d(a2),$16(a2)` and then the same `tst.l -$a(a6)` branch to 0x1A90E that 0x1AD6E makes.

0x1ad20.name: dispatch on d4 through the five-way table at 0x1AD38
0x1ad20.why: `cmpi.w #$4,d1` rejects anything above four straight to the tail, then `jmp $1ad38(pc,d1.w)` through a word table of relative offsets. The script opcode's sub-dispatch.

0x1ad42.name: subtract sign-extended field 0x5D from the word at 0x1C, and mark
0x1ad42.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d1; ext.w d1; sub.w d1,$1c(a2)` then `ori.b #$1,(a4)`, which is the tail 0x1ACE0 also branches to - so every write to that word raises the same flag bit.

0x1ad54.name: add field 0x5D of the record to field 0x19
0x1ad54.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d4; add.b d4,$19(a2); bra.w $1b048`. The additive sibling of 0x1ACEC, which copies rather than adds.

0x1ad60.name: add sign-extended field 0x5D to the word at 0x1A
0x1ad60.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d1; ext.w d1; add.w d1,$1a(a2)`. The additive sibling of 0x1ACF6.

0x1ad6e.name: add field 0x5D to field 0x16, and run 0x1A90E if the frame long is set
0x1ad6e.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d4; add.b d4,$16(a2)` then a `tst.l -$a(a6)`: zero takes the ordinary tail at 0x1B048, non-zero jumps to 0x1A90E instead.

0x1ad82.name: run the script's test and store the result in fields 0x5D and 0x5E
0x1ad82.why: the same call to 0x1A58A the branching cases make, but the byte it returns is written to both fields rather than tested.

0x1ad9a.name: read field 0x5D of the record and shift it right by d4
0x1ad9a.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d0; asr.b d4,d0; bra.b $1ada8` - a jump-table case whose whole content is which field it reads and that it shifts arithmetically.

0x1ada2.name: shift field 0x5D of the record left by d4
0x1ada2.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d0; asl.b d4,d0; move.b d0,$5d(a2)` - and the store is the tail 0x1AD9A branches to, so the right shift there writes the field back through this instruction.

0x1adb0.name: run the script's test and skip a longword when it is zero
0x1adb0.why: the same call as 0x1ADCC; a non-zero result carries on reading the script, a zero one does `addq.l #$4,$4(a2)` first - stepping the cursor past the four bytes of the branch it did not take.

0x1adcc.name: run the script's test and branch on any non-zero result
0x1adcc.why: pushes the record and d4, calls 0x1A58A, and takes the loop back to 0x1ABF6 - the script reader - only when the result is zero; otherwise 0x1ADC4. The three cases 0x1ADCC, 0x1ADE2 and 0x1ADF8 differ in nothing but the condition they branch on.

0x1ade2.name: run the script's test and branch when the result is negative
0x1ade2.why: identical to 0x1ADCC but for `bge.w` where that has `bne.b`, so this continues reading the script when the result is zero or positive.

0x1adf8.name: run the script's test and branch when the result is not negative
0x1adf8.why: identical to 0x1ADCC but for `blt.w`, the opposite of 0x1ADE2.

0x1ae0e.name: set field 0x5E to field 0x5D less the script's test result
0x1ae0e.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d3`, calls 0x1A58A, `sub.b d0,d3; move.b d3,$5e(a2)`. The computed sibling of 0x1AE2A, which subtracts d4 instead.

0x1ae2a.name: set field 0x5E to field 0x5D less d4
0x1ae2a.why: `move.b $5d(a2),d0; moveq #$0,d2; move.b d4,d2; sub.b d2,d0; move.b d0,$5e(a2)`.

0x1ae3c.name: set the channel's pitch from the note table, and the rest of the note opcodes
0x1ae3c.why: the main entry biases the note byte by the record's field 0x19, indexes the word table 0x3E36DE points at, and subtracts that from field 8 into field 0x22 - the pitch offset. Around it: field 0x5F set from d4, a guard on bit 7 of the note, a portamento path taken when field 0x13 is set and the frame long is non-zero, and 0x3E36FC selecting a second table. All of them leave through 0x1B048.

0x1b06e.name: look the note up in the table at 0x1EA3C, or take the bend
0x1b06e.why: masks the caller's word to four bits, indexes 0x1EA3C, and a 0xFF entry means there is no note there and the word at +0x5A of the record - the bend - is used instead.

0x1b166.name: count the four sample voices down and retrigger the ones that expire
0x1b166.why: only every eighth call - the byte at 0x3E3D6C counts down from 7. For each of the four bits of the mask byte, decrements that voice's word in the pair table at 0x3E3D72 and, when it reaches zero, writes the voice's byte from 0x1EA94 to the OKI port and reloads the counter with 5.

0x1b2b2.name: start the sample for a channel by writing its number to the OKI
0x1b2b2.why: walks the four bytes at 0x3E3D6E, indexing the ten-byte records at 0x1B674 by each, and on the first whose field +1 matches the requested channel writes that slot's byte from 0x1EA94 straight to 0x460000 - the OKI6295's command port.

0x1b306.name: start a channel: clear its counters and run its script
0x1b306.why: zeroes 0x3E3706, 0x3E36FA and 0x3E36EC, then runs the channel's script through 0x1A5F0.

0x1b42e.name: select the instrument the channel's byte names
0x1b42e.why: indexes the six-byte records at 0x19CE4 by the byte and stores the long it finds in 0x3E36DA, which is the instrument pointer every note lookup then reads.

0x1b4be.name: strobe the input latch and write the YM's address
0x1b4be.why: clears bit 0 of the shadow at 0x3E3D8E, writes it to 0x640000, sets the bit and writes again - a strobe - then works on the YM2413 at 0x480000.

0x1b538.name: play one channel's next event on the YM
0x1b538.why: clears 0x3E3708, then works through the channel's counters at 0x3E3706 and 0x3E370A with the flag at 0x3E36EC, writing to the YM2413 at 0x480000.

0x1b612.name: start every other channel of the type's pair, up to nine
0x1b612.why: takes the type's field +5 from the six-byte records at 0x19CE4, points 0x3E36DE at 0x19CF0, and adds one to the index when bit 0 of 0x3E36D4 is set. Then it walks two at a time to nine, calling 0x1B538 on each with the list head from 0x3E3D12.

0x1e7b8.name: emit two decoded bytes a row at a time, biased by d2
0x1e7b8.why: the same two-byte loop as 0x12574, but each byte has d2 added - the colour base - and the row stride is the fixed 0x1F8 with a count of 7 rather than a stride in d5.

0x1e7e4.name: expand one nibble pair across an eight-by-eight block
0x1e7e4.why: the high nibble of d0 is the repeat count and the low nibble plus d2 the value, written down a column with the 0x1F8 row stride and a count of 7. 0x1E804 below it is a separate entry doing the same expansion in place, rewriting each byte's low nibble from the caller's word.

0x1e834.name: fill an eight-by-four block of the playfield with one byte
0x1e834.why: four `move.b d0,(a1)+` under a `dbra` on d1, then `lea $1fc(a1),a1` to the next row and d1 reloaded, eight rows in all. 0x1FC plus the four bytes just written is the 0x200 stride.

0x1e862.name: decompress a byte as two hexadecimal digits
0x1e862.why: splits the byte at (a3) into nibbles, turns each into 0x30..0x39 or 0x41.. by adding 7 past 0x3A, biases by 0x13 and hands it to decompressTileId with 0x1B - so each nibble becomes the tile of its own digit. Loops on d3, so it renders a whole number.

0x1e8d2.name: halt with every interrupt masked, upper image
0x1e8d2.why: `stop #$2700` in the upper half of the image, reached separately from the overlay's 0x62e and 0x642.

0x1e8d6.name: the crash screen: freeze the machine and print its registers
0x1e8d6.why: masks every interrupt, clears the watchdog, pushes all sixteen registers, copies eight bytes of palette from 0x1E85A to 0x3C03E0 so there is something visible, and renders the register dump as hexadecimal from 0x203030 through 0x1E8C8. It does not return.

0x1e9b4.name: restart through the reset vector
0x1e9b4.why: `suba.l a0,a0; movea.l (a0)+,a7; movea.l (a0),a0; jmp (a0)` - the same restart as 0x133a6 without masking interrupts first.
